fatal_errors: The proposed PtPdRhRuIrOs ethanol-oxidation system does not match the target Pd@PtRuFeCoNi shell catalyst studied for HER and HOR.

Annealing-induced ordering is proposed as beneficial, whereas the target attributes activity and durability to the kinetically trapped, randomly mixed shell; heating produces L10/L12 ordering and ultimately phase separation.
The d-band-center/poisoning mechanism is not supported by the cited evidence and conflicts with E2's warning that a single d-band-center descriptor may be inadequate for heterogeneous HEA surfaces.

The falsification rule requires all predicted observables to be absent simultaneously; failure of ordering to reduce poisoning or improve durability despite an electronic shift would already refute the proposed causal chain.
explanation: There is only superficial overlap through multielement alloys, thermal treatment, and operando spectroscopy. The target concerns epitaxial PtRuFeCoNi atomic-layer shells on Pd nanocubes, with HER/HOR performance governed by site-specific H and OH adsorption, orbital hybridization, and metastable random mixing. The generated hypothesis instead addresses ethanol oxidation on a different six-element alloy and assigns durability to annealing-induced ordering and reduced poisoning. Its untreated baseline and paired operando experiment are reasonable for an independent study, but annealing would need controls for particle growth, facet changes, segregation, and surface-composition drift. E2 supports the relevance of the six-element alloy to ethanol oxidation but not the proposed ordering–d-band–durability mechanism, while E1 concerns NiFe OER phases and is essentially irrelevant.
